description: Add the two-stage deadline wrap-up protocol to OpenCodeRuntime: a per-turn deadline declaration on RuntimeTurnRequest (default 60 min, with.timeout override), a single fire-and-forget task-agnostic wrap-up warning injected via client.session.promptAsync() 5 minutes before the deadline (or at turn start when shorter), unchanged abort-on-deadline behaviour, no-abort when the warned turn ends on its own, and a real-OpenCode smoke record evidencing mid-turn promptAsync pickup.

tasks.title: Implement the two-stage deadline wrap-up protocol in OpenCodeRuntime (deadline declaration, warning scheduler, Action switchover, fake-clock tests)
tasks.description: Add an optional `deadlineMs?: number` to RuntimeTurnRequest in packages/runner/src/runtime/opencode/types.ts (omitted means no deadline, no warning, no internal timer). In packages/runner/src/runtime/opencode/turn.ts: when deadlineMs is declared, layer a timeout onto the external signal via the existing createTimeoutSignal helper from system/timeout-signal.ts (disposed in finally); export a DEADLINE_WARNING_TEXT constant and a WARNING_WINDOW_MS = 5*60*1000 constant; in executePrompt schedule exactly one setTimeout that fires at deadlineMs - WARNING_WINDOW_MS (or setTimeout(0) when deadlineMs <= WARNING_WINDOW_MS) and calls client.session.promptAsync() on the turn's physical Session with the warning body, fire-and-forget inside try/catch that emits an info-level RuntimeDiagnostic (code deadline-warning-injection-failed) on rejection and never fails/retries the turn; clear the timer in the same finally that disposes the timeout handle so a turn that completes before the warning is due never injects it. The existing abort path is unchanged: deadline reached while prompt is in flight calls client.session.abort() and returns interrupted; a turn whose prompt response arrived is not aborted regardless of whether the warning fired. In packages/runner/src/actions/opencode.ts: resolve the deadline via numberInput(context.with, "timeout") with DEFAULT_TURN_DEADLINE_MS = 60*60*1000 fallback, place it on the turn request, and do NOT surface the value in the prompt body, system variant, or any rendered variable.
acceptanceCriteria: RuntimeTurnRequest carries an optional deadlineMs: number field; existing callers that omit it behave exactly as before (no warning, no internal timer, external signal still honoured for cancel)

When deadlineMs is declared and > WARNING_WINDOW_MS, advancing vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(deadlineMs - WARNING_WINDOW_MS) results in client.session.promptAsync being called exactly once on the turn's physical Session with DEADLINE_WARNING_TEXT; advancing further to the deadline does not inject a second warning
When deadlineMs is declared and <= WARNING_WINDOW_MS, the warning is injected at turn start (setTimeout(0)) and is not injected a second time
When deadlineMs is undefined, client.session.promptAsync is never called by the runtime for that turn

When the awaited client.session.prompt() response arrives before the deadline (whether or not the warning fired), client.session.abort is NOT called for that Prompt execution and the normal completion facts are returned
When the deadline is reached while the prompt response has not arrived, client.session.abort is called once and the result kind is interrupted (unchanged from the pre-existing behaviour)
A rejected client.session.promptAsync call does NOT fail the turn and does NOT trigger a retry; exactly one info-level RuntimeDiagnostic with code deadline-warning-injection-failed is produced

DEADLINE_WARNING_TEXT is exported from turn.ts and asserts (via unit test) that it contains no marker names (unfinished, promise), no file names (progress.txt, *.md paths), and no task/profile identifiers

The mohist/opencode Action resolves deadlineMs from numberInput(context.with, "timeout") with a 60-minute default, places it on the turn request, and the prompt body / system variant / rendered variables contain no deadline value or static 'N minutes remaining' phrasing
All deadline-related tests use vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync; no test asserts on real elapsed wall-clock time, real setTimeout firing, or sleep/delay boundaries
The fake SDK client in packages/runner/tests/opencode-runtime-turn.spec.ts gains a sessionPromptAsync mock alongside sessionPrompt/sessionAbort, and the fakes use no internal setTimeout
npm run typecheck -w packages/runner and npm run test:run -w packages/runner pass
tasks.output: Extended RuntimeTurnRequest (deadlineMs), turn.ts warning scheduler + DEADLINE_WARNING_TEXT + WARNING_WINDOW_MS + layered createTimeoutSignal, opencode.ts Action deadline declaration, and fake-clock-driven unit tests in packages/runner/tests/opencode-runtime-turn.spec.ts (plus opencode-action-turn.spec.ts as needed)
tasks.notes: Design decisions D1-D6 in openspec/changes/issue-439/design.md. This is one cohesive feature module: the type, scheduler, Action switchover, and tests are intentionally merged per the task-splitting principles (interface + implementation + call-site + tests in one capability). Do NOT introduce a hand-rolled Clock abstraction; vi.useFakeTimers() is the sanctioned TS pattern per AGENTS.md. Reuse createTimeoutSignal from system/timeout-signal.ts — do not write a new timer primitive. The smoke record is a separate task (T-002) because it requires a real OpenCode environment and produces an artifact, not code.

tasks.title: Capture the real-OpenCode smoke record evidencing mid-turn promptAsync pickup
tasks.description: Run a one-time smoke against a real OpenCode server (CLI on PATH, pinned @opencode-ai/sdk version from #409) demonstrating that a client.session.promptAsync() message injected while a turn is running is picked up and processed by that turn at its next iteration boundary. Use a simple prompt that invokes a tool (e.g. a shell sleep or file read) so the iteration boundary is observable, inject the DEADLINE_WARNING_TEXT body mid-turn, and capture transcript evidence that the running turn processed the injected message (e.g. an assistant message or tool call referencing the warning). Record the OpenCode CLI/SDK version, the injected body, the session ID, the observed transcript evidence, and the wall-clock pickup latency. Persist the result as openspec/changes/issue-439/deadline-warning-smoke.json mirroring the format of openspec/changes/issue-409/sdk-smoke-verification.json.
acceptanceCriteria: The record captures the OpenCode CLI version, the pinned @opencode-ai/sdk version, the injected prompt body (matching DEADLINE_WARNING_TEXT from T-001), the running turn's session ID, and transcript evidence that the running turn processed the injected message
The record notes the wall-clock latency between promptAsync injection and observed pickup
The smoke is not wired into the default test suite (npm run test:run -w packages/runner does not invoke real OpenCode)
If the environment has no real OpenCode CLI available, the task records that fact explicitly in the JSON along with the asserted behaviour to verify, and does not fabricate evidence
tasks.output: openspec/changes/issue-439/deadline-warning-smoke.json capturing real-OpenCode mid-turn promptAsync pickup evidence
tasks.notes: Design decision D7. The issue body states mid-turn steering is already verified; this task records the evidence in the change's artifact directory so the acceptance criterion '冒烟记录' is satisfied. Requires a real OpenCode CLI in the execution environment; if absent, record the gap honestly rather than skipping or fabricating. The smoke is verification evidence only — never re-run as part of npm test.
